questions.short_title: Digital support pathway for OHCA bystanders feasible
questions.question: In the RescQ evaluation of a digital support pathway for bystanders of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, what proportion of registered adult bystanders actually used the digital resources at least once?
options: About 10%
About two thirds
About half
questions.explanation: Registered adults engaged with the pathway at very high rates, which supports its feasibility. But this came from a single-region evaluation where only about half of eligible incidents were captured, so it is context rather than proof of a standard model.

questions.short_title: Extrication after road collisions: an evidence map
questions.question: What was the main reason this scoping review couldn't draw firm conclusions about extrication effectiveness?
options: Most studies excluded the most severely injured patients
Entrapment was too rare to measure any outcome
Only volunteer data were available for clinical outcomes
Definitions and outcomes were reported inconsistently across studies
questions.explanation: The review found fragmented definitions of entrapment, extrication method and time, plus heterogeneous outcome reporting, which blocked pooled analysis and system-level learning. It's a scoping review, so it maps the evidence rather than testing whether any approach works.

questions.short_title: Updated paediatric traumatic arrest position statement
questions.question: How does the position statement view compressions and ventilations in paediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest compared with adults?
options: They are of no value unless bystander CPR was given
They have a smaller role, as haemorrhage dominates paediatric arrest
They have a larger role, since causes like hypoxia and head injury are more common
They should only be started after bilateral chest decompression
questions.explanation: The statement says compressions and ventilations have a larger role in paediatric than adult traumatic arrest, with children often arresting from head injury, hypoxia and other non-haemorrhagic causes. As US consensus guidance, withholding and termination decisions still follow your local CPGs.

questions.short_title: Choking arrests: ROSC common, survival still poor
questions.question: Compared with presumed cardiac arrests, choking-related out-of-hospital cardiac arrests were notable for what pattern?
options: Better survival to discharge as well as more prehospital ROSC
Higher rates of prehospital ROSC, but similar survival to discharge
No difference in prehospital ROSC or survival
Lower rates of prehospital ROSC but comparable survival
questions.explanation: Prehospital ROSC was much more common in FBAO arrests (62.7% vs 37.8%), yet survival to discharge was similar (10.6% vs 9.0%). The registry coding of 'obviously FBAO-related' wasn't independently verified, so treat this as exploratory.

questions.short_title: Liberal ambulance fluids did not reduce sepsis mortality
questions.question: In the PITSTOP-Fluids trial, liberal prehospital fluids (median 1500 mL) versus usual care (median 500 mL) for suspected sepsis had what effect on hospital mortality?
options: Mortality was essentially identical between the two groups
Usual care had higher mortality from undertreated hypotension
Liberal fluids reduced mortality by about 20%
The benefit only appeared in patients over 76 years
questions.explanation: Hospital mortality was 18.0% with liberal fluids versus 18.3% with usual care, with all secondary outcomes similar. The trial excluded the sickest patients and even usual care gave most a bolus, so it supports current practice rather than mandating more fluid.

questions.short_title: Clinician smartphones linked to tripled interpreter use
questions.question: What change was linked to the tripling of virtual interpreter use in this study?
options: Offering interpreters in a wider range of languages
Switching from audio-only to video interpreter services
Replacing heavy laptops with lightweight agency-issued smartphones
Introducing a mandatory interpreter checklist on every job
questions.explanation: Requests per 100 encounters rose from 0.19 to 0.57 after clinicians were issued lightweight smartphones instead of laptops. It was a pre-post design, so other workflow changes could have contributed and there were no patient outcome data.

questions.short_title: A US systems approach to MCI triage
questions.question: In the systems approach to mass-casualty triage described in this review, why is ongoing retriage emphasised?
options: To identify which ambulance service each casualty belongs to
To move patients away from the incident command post
To confirm which patients need a transport officer
To reduce overtriage as casualty conditions change
questions.explanation: The review describes dynamic primary, secondary and tertiary triage with repeated retriage so patients are reassessed as conditions change, minimising overtriage. It's a narrative US review, so treat it as context rather than evidence.

questions.short_title: Paramedic students learn safety from unsafe events
questions.question: In this qualitative study of paramedic students, what role did unsafe or difficult clinical situations play in learning about patient safety?
options: They improved learning only when formally debriefed by clinical supervisors
They acted as learning triggers, shaped by role modelling, feedback and emotional processing
They were mainly avoided, as students felt unprepared to process them
They had no lasting impact on students' future professional practice
questions.explanation: Unsafe situations served as triggers for learning, but that learning depended on supervisory responses, feedback and reflection on the emotional impact. Keep in mind this was self-reported student narratives with no follow-up on actual outcomes.
